headline: Approved farm property tax exemption ordinance, $50,000 John Street Bridge egress study funds, and Parade Grounds bicycle racks.
summary: Members approved an ordinance on property tax exemptions for farm machinery and farm buildings, 7-1 with one absent. They also approved a $50,000 appropriation for the John Street Bridge egress study grant match, a new Safety and Risk Management Coordinator job description, and two bicycle racks on the Parade Grounds. Members also discussed sidewalks, a possible consolidated high school, and how to handle public email forwarding requests.
decisions: Approved consent agenda items 3a through 3d and 3f by voice vote, with Councilor Tatta recused from item 3c.
Approved an ordinance concerning property tax exemption for certain farm machinery and farm buildings, 7-1 with one absent.
Approved a new job description for Safety and Risk Management Coordinator, 6-2 with one absent.
Approved a $50,000 appropriation from CAP & NON, Fund 301 to the Industrial Egress Study expense account, 8-0 with one absent.
Approved the placement of bicycle racks on the Parade Grounds, 6-2 with one absent.

Thomas Laffin, Jesse Reynolds, Melanie Rossacci (remote), Christina Tatta and Chairman Vincent F. 
Testa, Jr. Mayor Vincent Cervoni, Town Attorney Geoffrey Einhorn, Comptroller Tim Sena and Acting

2. Roll Call

Youth Sector Representative and Diane Tourangeau, Coalition for Better Wallingford board member 
addressed the Council. Red Ribbon Week is the oldest drug prevention campaign, celebrated every year 
from October 23 – October 31.  The main goal being to encourage a drug-free lifestyle and spread 
awareness.  They encourage everyone to participate in their upcoming events.

 5. PUBLIC QUESTION & ANSWER PERIOD  
 
 
Larry Kellog addressed the Council and gave thanks for the painting of crosswalks that was completed.

 6. Chairman’s Update 
 a.  Golden Fox Theatre 
 b.  Parker Farms/Route 150 Intersection

Chairman Testa asked for the Chairman’s Update so he could specifically address these items.  (a) 
Mayor stated there has been no change since the last meeting with Golden Fox Theatre.  (b) As 
discussed in Public Question & Answer Period with Larry Kellogg, crosswalks have been painted. (c)

7.        To conduct a public hearing to consider and act on an ordinance concerning Property Tax       
           Exemption for Certain Farm Machinery and Farm Buildings – Law Dept.  
 
Corporation Counsel Janis Small and Wallingford Tax Assessor Kevin Coons addressed the Council.  
Legislature increased the number of allowable exemptions, and the ordinance is proposing to make those 
increases.  Kevin Coons stated there are 10 farming organizations in Wallingford that would benefit 
from this program.  They are looking to increase the exemption to $250,000 on farm equipment and 
$500,000 on farm buildings.   Councilor Fishbein asked to clarify if this is an exemption and not a 
deferral.  Mr. Coons stated that it is an exemption.  Currently, if a building is assessed exclusively for 
farm use and it’s assessed at $250,000, the first $100,00 would be exempt and the difference would be

taxable.  This ordinance would also benefit local vineyards.  Councilor Tatta asked what the amount of 
taxes would be that the town would forego if the ordinance was passed.  Mr. Coons calculated a little 
over $80,000 in tax revenue.  Councilor Carmody expressed his support to our farms and wants to make 
sure the program is available to all who qualify.  Councilor Reynolds would like to help reduce costs to

He’s happy we are maxing out what Wallingford can do, in this case.

Human Resources Director Jim Hutt and Risk Manager Kurt Treiber addressed the Council seeking 
approval of a job description for Safety and Risk Management Coordinator with an annual salary range 
of $85,431 - $108,409.  The position was presented to the Council during fiscal year 2027 budget and 
was approved by the Council with a funding of six months.  The filling of the position would not be 
until January 2027. 
 
Councilor Fishbein asked about the new position and participating in meetings in a hybrid capacity or 
attending in person.  Mr. Hutt stated that is a management decision.  Councilor Fishbein feels it makes 
sense to be more specific on this topic.   
 
Councilor Rossacci asked if the job would include inspections on current construction projects in town.  
Mr. Hutt clarified they would be inspecting existing buildings not construction related inspections. 
 
Councilor Tatta asked if this position is being created for the purpose of succession planning.  Mr. Hutt 
explained that that is a small part of it, as the current management in Human Resources will be retiring 
in the next 5 years.  Councilor Tatta expressed concern over creating a new union position, as once 
created, it will be there forever. 
 
Councilor Fishbein asked what portion of the description says that this individual would not inspect 
construction projects.  Mr. Hutt explained they tried to make the description as broad as possible.  The 
position is not for a trained Engineer or Construction Inspector.  The applicant will need to be familiar 
with worker’s compensation, safety and risk.   
 
Councilor Tatta asked for clarification on the salary range and what the total cost would be, including 
benefits.  Mr. Hutt explained that it would depend on what class size they are for insurance and if they 
even take our insurance.  The applicant may be in a position where insurance is not needed and would 
not be a cost to the town. 
 
Councilor Fishbein asked for clarification on the word “considerable” in the job description and what 
constitutes something to be considerable.  Mr. Hutt explained that the person being hired may have 
experience in one aspect and less in another.  The individual would be given experience to grow on the 
job.

Chairman Testa asked Sheila Tierney to speak on the sidewalks as she did not have the opportunity 
during the Chairman’s Report.  Ms. Tierney asked for an update and specific guidelines that constitute a

9. Discussion and possible action regarding tentative agreement for successor pension contract 
between Town of Wallingford and Local 1570, AFSCME effective from July 1, 2026 to October 
13, 2029 – Human Resources  
 
Human Resources Director Jim Hutt addressed the Council seeking approval of a 3-year pension 
contract extension with the Police Union Local 1570 of ASME from July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2029.  
There are few changes to the language pertaining to the IRS code that was provided by the town’s 
pension attorney.  There are no substantive changes to the benefit.   
 
10. Consider and approve Appropriation of funds in the amount of $50,000 from CAP & NON, Fund 
301 to Exp.-Industrial Egress Study, Acct. #30102027-57000-TBD – Economic Development  
 
MOTION WAS MADE TO approve an appropriation of funds in the amount of $50,000 from 
CAP & NON, Fund 301 to Exp.-Industrial Egress Study, Acct #30102027-57000. 
 
 MADE BY: CARMODY  
SECONDED BY: REYNOLDS  
 
Economic Development Specialist Don Crouch addressed the Council.  The Town of Wallingford is 
pursuing a $250,000 Economic Development Administration Grant for the John Street Bridge egress and 
resiliency planning.  The request is for a 20% match required by the $250,000 grant. The purpose of the 
grant is to help address needs assessment feasibility analysis on what will be required to be replaced or 
enhanced on the John Street Bridge and create a viable alternate access and egress routes, potential 
economic impacts on bridge disruption and impacts on large businesses such as Amazon, Ulbrich Steel 
and Wallingford Public Utilities. 
 
Councilor Tatta expressed appreciation for this item on the Agenda.  She asked about a plan to extend 
the road to go out to Toelles Rd and then connect directly to exit 13 on ramp.  Mr. Crouch confirmed 
that this would be part of the grant.

11.  Consider and approve the placement of bicycle racks on the Parade Grounds – Mayor  
 
MOTION WAS MADE TO approve the placement of bicycle racks on the Parade Grounds. 
 
MADE BY: CARMODY  
SECONDED BY: REYNOLDS  
 
Economic Development Specialist Don Crouch and Town Planner Kevin Pagini addressed the Council.   
Mr. Pagini explained we have been working with Connecticut Main Street to identify ways to initiate  
more walkability in downtown Wallingford and provide alternatives for cyclists to secure their bikes on  
bicycle racks instead of light poles.  We have been working with Wallingford Center Inc to determine  
the location of the 13 new bicycle racks from the historic train station park to the Parade Grounds and  
across to Simpson Court.  Bicycle rack options include artistic, engraved bicycle racks that say  
Wallingford, bicycle racks that look like bicycles, and standard slotted U-shaped bicycle racks, in the  
colors of red and yellow.  Approval is needed from the Council to place two bicycle racks on the Parade  
Grounds.  Installation will be completed and donated by Choate Rosemary Hall.

Councilor Tatta expressed displeasure with the color choice and would have preferred Hunter Green to  
match the esthetic of downtown Wallingford. 
 
Councilor Fishbein asked for an explanation of Connecticut Main Street and their organization.  Mr.  
Crouch explained that Connecticut Main Street meets with Wallingford Center Inc and the Town  
Planner to analyze how we are doing as a town and a community for the downtown.  We have been  
ranked in the top 10 most walkable downtowns.  There was discussion on the placement of the bicycle  
racks which would be between the road and the sidewalk.  Councilor Fishbein stated he wished Council  
had been a part of discussion from the beginning to pick the colors. 
 
Barbara Kapi asked about the impact of the bicycle racks and the events held on the Parade Grounds put  
on by Wallingford’s Public Celebration Committee.  Chairman Testa explained there would be no  
impact on the events.  The Council could restrict cyclists from riding through the event like they request  
no dog walking during events.

12. Presentation from Chief Timothy Wall regarding new State Statutes authorizing additional 
EMT/Firefighter tax abatements and/or exemptions – Chairman Testa  
 
Councilor Tatta recused herself from the discussion. 
 
Volunteer Fire Chief Tim Wall and William Celata from Volunteer Fire Chief Company 8 addressed the  
Council.  In doing research for initiatives and benefits for the volunteer fire service, EMT’s and police  
officers, General Statues 1281W and 1281X were brought to attention.  Chief. Wall and Chief. Celata  
are asking the Council to consider General Statute 1281X for property tax abatement for the surviving  
spouse of a police officer, firefighter, or emergency medical technician who has died in the line of duty.

Chief Wall wanted to bring this to the Council’s attention and determine the next course of action.   
Chairman Testa explained the next course of action would be to forward to the Ordinance Committee for  
review.  Councilor Reynolds, Chairman of the Ordinance Committee advised the next meeting would be  
the 1st Tuesday of December.   
 
13. Discussion regarding the status of the potential consolidated high school as it relates to possible 
Town Council action – Councilor Tatta  
 
Councilor Tatta stated that she, Councilor Fishbein, Councilor Carmody and Councilor Rossacci  
have asked for this item to be placed on the agenda to update the public on the Council’s role in the  
consolidation of the high schools.  This is a big issue in town and the councilors wanted to clarify that  
there is no action that can be voted on by the Council until they are presented with something from the  
Board of Education.  Another issue is how the money the project would be appropriated.  If the Mayor  
vetoes but the Council approves, does the project move forward?  Lastly, the issue of a referendum to  
vote on the consolidation of the high schools. 
 
Councilor Laffin has been advocating for a referendum.  He feels this is a decision that should be voted  
on by the community. 
 
Councilor Carmody acknowledged the project is a huge undertaking and feels we should have  
transparency as much as possible.  He supports a referendum, so the people have a chance to vote. 
 
Councilor Rossacci would like to open up the Charter.  She feels large projects like this should  
automatically go to referendum. 
 
Councilor Fishbein addressed the short time frame we have to go through the process of initiating a  
referendum. 
 
Councilor Reynolds is in favor of a townwide referendum to make a decision.  He feels regardless of a  
time frame, if an issue is important to an individual, they will show up to vote in November.   
 
14.  Discussion and possible action on developing a standard operating procedure for town staff to 
follow when they have received a communication from a member of the public including a 
forwarding directive intending dissemination to the Town Council, as well as to possibly others – 
Councilor Fishbein  
 
Councilor Fishbein wanted to discuss directives from the public to forward email communications to the  
Town Council or other departments.  As well as respond to the requestor that their email has been  
forwarded.  He feels this could create a problem if an email was inadvertently not forwarded to Council  
or a certain department.  If a member of the public emails pictures of sidewalks needing repair and the  
email was not properly forwarded, this could put the clerk in the middle of being a witness to the notice.   
He would like to alleviate the possibility of that.

Mayor clarified that the Charter states the Town Clerk is the clerk of the Town Council.  The Council 
has the authority to direct the Town Clerk. If a resident has an issue, it should be up to the Town Council 
to direct the clerk on how to handle that request.  There are certain notices that go to the Town Clerk by 
statute and must follow a statutory procedure.  If it is a matter of filing a Claim against the town, that 
would be directed to the Town Clerk’s office. 
 
Acting Town Clerk Leanna Gnazzo addressed the Council with an example of a resident asking for an 
email to be forwarded to Council and any other relevant departments.  Also, emails asking for personal 
email contact information for Boards and Commissions.  Ms. Gnazzo stated she did not feel comfortable 
making assumptions and would not forward to unspecified departments and would not give out personal 
information.  She advised the resident to contact the Commission directly and they would provide the 
information to the members. 
 
Corporation Counsel Janis Small added that the Town Clerks does not answer for other departments and 
doing so makes her the middleman.  Since the Town Clerk is acting as the Council’s secretary, it would 
be appropriate for the Council to advise on how to handle those scenarios.
